The conventional-cell lattice is the near-ambient measurement of the EOS specimen in Ross and Angel (1999). Fractional coordinates are symmetry-equivalent representatives of Sasaki et al.'s Pbnm CaTiO3 refinement, which Ross and Angel identify as consistent with their structure. The four occupied Wyckoff orbits give Ca4Ti4O12 (Z=4). The numerical 298 K EOS reference is an operational encoding of the source's qualitative room-temperature statement, not a reported thermometer reading.

## Ross and Angel (1999), single-crystal BM3

`calcium_titanate_perovskite_ross_1999_bm3_1` · Executable

Reproduction: **reproduced** · [Reconstruction report](../reconstruction-reports/calcium_titanate_perovskite.md#record-calcium_titanate_perovskite_ross_1999_bm3_1)

**Source finding:** Coefficients from the abstract and Results (page 279), fitted to the 11 Table 1 observations with pressures from quartz volumes (Angel et al. (1997)). The standard Eulerian convention is confirmed by the source's 0.03 GPa maximum residual and weighted chi-square of 1.4.
